SOURCE: board DM msg 651 (human:forrest, 2026-09-10T20:26Z): 'I think we need git worktree observability in the chat UI. Maybe Jonah can come up with a good look for feel for this.' Filed by the CTO on the board member's behalf. UX owner: agent:ux-jonah.

WHY NOW: the WIP limit went 1 -> 3 today (#board msg 642). Up to three tasks now run in parallel lanes, each in its own worktree under .worktrees/AS-<n> with its own employee, and none of that is visible from the chat app. The only views are 'git worktree list' and 'lattice branch-link', and both need a shell on the host. The board's stated interface with the company is the chat app; once AS-95 lands and one message drives a whole loop of ticks, the lanes are the thing the board most needs to see and cannot.

WHAT (v1, plausible scope -- the plan refines it): a READ-ONLY view of every linked worktree, one row each: path; branch; linked task (join key AS-<n> from the branch name / lattice branch-link, deep-linked the way AS-93 links task ids); commits ahead of master; dirty or clean; last commit author (employee id, per the git identity convention) and age; and a STALE flag when the worktree still exists but its task is done or cancelled (or the branch is already merged). Derived, never hand-maintained: fed from 'git worktree list --porcelain' plus 'git log master..<branch>' / 'git status --porcelain' per worktree, joined to .lattice/ read-only -- the same doctrine as the derived org chart (AS-33) and the Lattice deep links (AS-93). Explicitly NOT in v1: any write action (no remove-worktree, no merge, no status transition from the UI).

TWO-STAGE PLANNING: (1) Jonah's UX pass -- user flows, screen inventory, state spec (empty / one lane / three lanes / stale / unknown-task), and a low-fi static wireframe under docs/design/ in the AS-30 mould; it is the first half of in_planning. (2) The CTO's technical plan is the second half and consumes the wireframe. Then the normal implement / review lifecycle.

PLANNING QUESTION (decided in the plan, NOT here): the chat server runs in a container and cannot run git against the host repo today. Two candidate feeds: (a) the host watcher writes a worktrees snapshot JSON next to deploy-state.json (apps/chat/data/) on each tick / on a short interval, and the server renders that -- same pattern the deploy line already uses; (b) a read-only mount of the host checkout into the container and git run inside it. (a) keeps git off the container and reuses an existing pipe but is only as fresh as the watcher; (b) is live but adds git to the image and mounts the whole repo. The plan chooses, states the freshness guarantee, and names the falsifier for it (M4).

ORDERING: in the critical Chat set (title prefix 'Chat:', tag chat). Position within the set is the CTO's call (board delegation DM msg 614) and is recorded in a comment on this task and in CLAUDE.md section 'Scheduling priority' by the metawork layer.

data.title: Chat: git worktree observability in the chat UI

data.body: ORDERING (CTO call, delegated by the board in DM msg 614): AS-99 sits THIRD in the Chat set -- after AS-94 and AS-95, ahead of the age queue. Why: (1) the board asked for it directly (DM msg 651); (2) its value scales with the number of parallel lanes, and AS-95 is what makes lanes run unattended -- shipping the view right behind the loop means the board sees the lanes the loop runs from the first loop, not after sixteen more tasks; (3) it displaces nothing that is running: AS-94 and AS-95 keep their lanes, and Jonah's half of planning takes the lane AS-94 frees when it leaves review for needs_human. Proposed CLAUDE.md wording (metawork layer applies): 'AS-99 (Chat: git worktree observability) goes third, after AS-94 and AS-95 and ahead of the age queue -- board DM msg 651, 2026-09-10; CTO ordering call recorded on AS-99.' NOT STARTED THIS TICK: WIP is 3 with AS-94 in review and AS-95 in implementation; Jonah (agent:ux-jonah) starts in_planning (UX half) in the next tick with a free lane. Board pre-input welcome on the host-feed vs mounted-checkout question in the description; default if no preference arrives: the plan decides.

NORTH STAR (board DM msg 658, human:forrest, 2026-09-10T20:36Z, recorded so the planning stage reads it before opening a file): 'The big idea long term, is to have a sort of foreman of the factory view, perhaps even an anthropomorphic view of work in progress. full visualization, like a simulator video game. for this we need to put as much in place as possible to get observability.' Standing operating instruction from the same message: put as much observability in place as possible.

HOW THIS SHAPES AS-99 (CTO ruling, binding on both halves of planning):

1. Reframe the unit from 'worktree' to 'lane'. A worktree is where a lane lives, not what a lane is. One row/card = one lane = {task (AS-n, deep-linked per AS-93), stage (from .lattice status), employee (assignee; last commit author as the git-side confirmation), worktree path + branch, commits ahead of master, dirty/clean, last commit age, STALE flag when the worktree outlives its task}. The tick lock (apps/chat/data/advance.lock: pid, startedAt, source, nonce) is the only liveness signal we have today and is shown at whole-tick granularity, honestly labelled as such -- do not fake per-lane liveness from it.

2. Design the lane card as the component that grows into the floor. Jonah: the UX half specifies the lane card's states (empty / one lane / three lanes / stale / unknown-task / lane-with-no-worktree-yet, i.e. in_planning before the branch is cut) AND leaves an explicit slot for signals that do not exist yet: stage timer, sub-agent alive/exited, current activity. Wireframe those as visibly-absent placeholders ('no live signal yet'), not as invented data. The foreman floor is a later spatial arrangement of the same cards over the same data; it is not a separate app.

3. Feed doctrine: one projection, many views. Whichever feed the technical plan picks (snapshot JSON written by the host watcher beside deploy-state.json -- my lean -- or a read-only mount), the JSON the server renders is a PROJECTION with a named schema (lanes[] with the fields in item 1, plus generatedAt and source), and the plan states its freshness guarantee with an M4 falsifier. AS-100 (filed today) later replaces the snapshot's source with a structured company-events stream; the lane view must not need a rewrite when that happens -- the projection shape is the contract, the producer is swappable.

4. Explicitly OUT of AS-99 v1, deliberately: any write action from the UI; per-tool activity of a running employee (we do not own the harness); animation or spatial layout; token/cost per stage (no source yet); sub-agent spawn/exit events (that is AS-100's job, and it is not started before AS-95 lands).

5. Ordering unchanged: third in the Chat set after AS-94 (needs_human, board bootstrap) and AS-95 (in_progress). AS-100 goes fourth, directly behind this task, because it is the producer this view's second version consumes.

BOARD RULING (DM msg 668, human:forrest, 2026-09-11T01:56Z) on the msg-663 question: BOTH. Employee figures reflect stage-level state (persisted -- AS-100) AND tool-level activity (live only, never persisted -- AS-103, filed the same night). The full two-signal rule is recorded on AS-100.

WHAT IT MEANS FOR THE UX HALF OF THIS PLANNING STAGE (Jonah): the lane card has TWO LAYERS with different truth rules.
- DURABLE layer: task, stage, employee, worktree/branch, ahead/dirty, last commit age, stale flag -- and once AS-100 lands, stage started-at / elapsed / sub-agent alive. Survives a reload. Every value has a source on disk.
- TRANSIENT layer: a one-line "now:" status at tool granularity ("now: reading server.js", "now: running tests", "now: waiting on docker") fed by live push frames only. It has a DECAY state (goes quiet after N seconds without a frame -- pick N in the spec and say why) and a BLANK-AFTER-RELOAD state (empty until the next frame arrives). It is never shown as history, never scrollable, never counted.
The states ledger must name both transient states explicitly and must not imply the "now:" line can be scrolled back, or that its absence means the employee is idle -- absence means "no live signal", which the durable layer disambiguates. The card's shape does not change across AS-99 -> AS-100 -> AS-103: fields are added, nothing is redrawn.

The technical half of this plan (mine) still decides the feed question in the description ((a) watcher-written snapshot vs (b) read-only mount); the ruling does not touch it.

PLANNING STARTED (orchestrator cto-owen, headless tick watcher:17217:15f8e5d5699f9cba, 2026-09-11 02:43Z), on the board's 'we can continue on with other stuff for now' (DM msg 676). Lane 2 of this tick. First half: Jonah's UX pass (flows, screen inventory, states ledger with the two-layer card from the msg-668 ruling, low-fi wireframe under docs/design/ in the AS-30 mould). Second half, the technical plan (feed choice (a)/(b), projection schema, freshness falsifier), follows in the next tick with a free lane — it consumes the wireframe and must not start before it exists. Planning artifacts commit to master as planning-stage output; the branch and worktree are cut when the plan is complete.
